summary: Sequenced delta audit delivery with gap-detection, per-tenant manifest, and TTL provenance proof
description: Customer requests a certified delivery pattern for audit events used in regulatory forensics. They want incremental (delta) batches that are strictly ordered per-tenant with a manifest that proves sequence continuity, gap detection metadata, and TTL provenance for legal hold and retention verification. The deliverable should include a sample delivery to Azure Event Hubs and an S3 fallback with signed manifests (RFC 3161 timestamping or equivalent) and an explanation of how KMS-wrapped signing keys are rotated.
impact: Customer's compliance team is unable to complete their inbound SOC or audit because they cannot demonstrate chain-of-custody and ordered delivery guarantees. They have paused a scheduled audit until we supply an attested sample. Business impact: potential delay in contract renewal and elevated legal scrutiny.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer configured tenant-level webhook to our audit export endpoint. 2) Expected strictly ordered event batches with sequence_number per tenant. 3) Observed reordering and occasional missed sequence numbers across two business days. 4) Customer attempted replays and saw duplicate offsets from our S3 fallback manifest. 5) Customer requests a reproducible sample and artifact demonstrating gap detection and reconciliation behavior.
sample_payload_request: Customer requests (a) 10-minute sample of delta bundles for tenant 'finovia-prod' in prod.us-east, (b) JSON manifest format with sequence_number, prev_hash, batch_hash, rfc3161_tstamp, and kms_key_id, (c) a redaction flag for PII fields and sample mapping for the customer's QRadar ingestion (field mappings and overflow policy). Provide the sample both as Azure Event Hubs push and as signed S3 objects.

investigation_notes:
- Initial triage: observed intermittent delivery backpressure in the webhook router during the time window; two 429 spikes recorded in the router metrics.
- Correlated with autoscaling events: dedicated delivery worker pool scaled from 4->2 briefly due to throttling logic threshold.
- Manifest generation job uses best-effort accumulation window; when delivery worker retries out-of-order, manifest prev_hash may not reflect final persisted order.
- Identified missing invariant: manifest creation currently assumes idempotent append but does not enforce strict sequence-lock during concurrent batch flushes.
- Reproduced locally by simulating concurrent batch flush with artificially delayed KVS persistence; observed the same gap pattern and duplicate offset in fallback manifest.
proposed_workaround: 1) Temporarily enable per-tenant sequence-lock mode for finovia-prod to force a single writer path (console toggle). 2) Advise customer to hold audit replay until we provide attested sample. 3) Provide manual reconciliation manifest covering the requested window with signed timestamps and explicit gap markers.
resolution: (pending) Engineering has a prioritized patch to add a lightweight sequence-lock for manifest flushes and to include explicit gap-detection entries in manifests. SRE will generate the requested attested sample for 2025-02-16 09:10-09:20 window and deliver via secure S3 presigned link plus Event Hubs test push. Will include RFC-3161 style timestamping via our timestamping proxy and a key-rotation note. Target delivery: 2025-02-20.
